lines: One developer. Four projects. Four AI agents, all working at the same time.
And not even a usage limit stops the work.
Two run Claude Code. Two run Codex.
I give each one a clear task, then rotate. Plan, review, next window.
Every project has written context. Requirements, architecture, design, memory, rules, and a tracker.
So the agent follows decisions, instead of guessing.
But what happens when one agent hits its usage limit, mid task?
The limit isn't the real problem. Losing the context is.

lines.say: I run my switch provider skill.

lines: It finishes a safe checkpoint, and writes a handoff. The goal, decisions, changed files, real test results, and next steps.
It saves that to private project memory, scans it for secrets, and then I type exit.

lines.t: The launcher asks: Subscription, or OpenRouter, with a spending cap I set. I choose. Not the agent.
lines.say: The launcher asks. Subscription, or Open Router, with a spending cap I set. I choose. Not the agent.

lines: The new session reads the checkpoint, and the work just continues.
Same skill, in Claude Code and Codex. That's how you ship faster in the AI era.
